title: One of a Kind
paragraphs: "What are you talking about?"

That's strange. As far as I know, Panda used to do that kind of work with Keel, even though he hated it. I remember him saying he didn't want to do it, but deep down, it was actually the kind of work he wanted to do.

As we chatted like that on our way there, we passed through the zoo and arrived at the mansion. A staff member came out to greet us. Then we were asked to wait inside the mansion. Father was looking at something that resembled a culture capsule set up inside the mansion, together with Sakura-chan.
“I thought it was just like a zoo, but places like this really do feel like another world.”
“You’re absolutely right.”

When the Doctor came to the village, there was equipment like this in the research lab, too. Back in the first world, Father and the others had also modified the bio-plants to make them more convenient.
“The last time I was here, while we were waiting like this, I talked with Father about how it looked like research facilities from a disaster movie.”

“That’s exactly right—it doesn’t seem like something you could joke about. The zoo section is practically like a dinosaur park, isn’t it? If an accident were to happen… I’m sure we could easily escape.”
“Hmm? Escape?”
“No, not exactly. But in my world, there are a lot of stories where dangerous research like this leads to accidents.”
“Huh.”
“Do accidents actually happen?”
Yuki-chan asks Father.
“I think it’ll be fine? But typically, it’s the kind of scenario where monsters go on a rampage.”
“They didn’t strike me as the type to do something so reckless. They really cherished this place.”

“Maybe being able to talk to monsters takes the edge off the tension. That said, the scary ones in this kind of scenario are probably bacterial zombies or research that destroys a monster’s sense of self, right?”
“I hear a voice hoping for some kind of bizarre accident.”
The Doctor appeared at just the right moment. Were you eavesdropping or something?
“That sort of thing is caused by dreamers who lack understanding, or researchers who haven’t built trust with their test subjects.”
“Uh, uh… I’m sorry.”
“It’s fine. I know full well that few people will understand anyway. Welcome to my office—are you the party of the Shield and Spear Heroes?”

“Yes. My name is Naofumi Iwatani, and I was summoned as the Shield Hero. The one holding the spear is Motoyasu Kitamura, the Spear Hero. We’re also joined by Ms. Rasazusa, a Guardian Knight of Siltvelt, and Mr. Werner, the representative of the Shusaku species.”

Then Father spreads his arms wide, as if to introduce Sakura-chan and the others. Oh, so he’s giving Sakura-chan and the others special treatment! Well, that’s only natural. Though, if anything, it might be because their Doctor happens to be a monster enthusiast.
“And these children are Filolials who have transformed thanks to being raised by the Heroes.”
“Nice to meet you.”
“Hmm…”
“H-hello.”
One by one, Yuki and the others greet Father as he instructs them.
“Thank you for coming all this way. My name is Ratotille Anthreya. Close friends call me Rat. I’m the representative here, for what it’s worth.”
The Doctor replied to us in a welcoming tone.
“So? What brings you here? If you’d like me to examine those children, I’d be happy to do so.”
“This one’s skills are top-notch. However, I’d prefer you avoid any forceful examinations.”
“That depends on my interest. That said, a Filolial that’s taking human form is certainly a subject of interest.”
With keen interest, the Doctor stares intently at Yuki-chan.
“Yuki-chan, if you struggle, they’ll drug you so you can’t move, so you’d better behave.”
“O-okay! As a noble being, I’ll make sure not to act in an unladylike manner in a setting like this.”
That’s Yuki-chan for you. Her overflowing nobility really shines through.
“Very well, then. Please refrain from conducting the examination too forcefully.”
“Yes, yes. I get it.”

With that, the Doctor began examining Yuki-chan. Along the way, he had Yuki-chan return to her Filolial form and did various other things, but even after she struggled, he didn’t end up drugging her. As expected, the Doctor is someone who can be reasoned with.
“Well, just from seeing the first one, I had a general idea, but she’s the picture of health.”
“Yuki-chan, you were such a good girl—you stayed still.”
“Yes. Motoyasu-sama, Yuki has accomplished her mission.”
“Hmm…”
Sakura-chan furrowed her brow slightly, and Kou looked a bit uncomfortable. They look like they’d rather not do this, don’t they?
“Both of you, calm down. If you don’t struggle, the doctor will be able to examine you properly.”
“But—…”
“Nooo—”
Maybe they’re instinctively afraid of doctors. But this is all for Sakura-chan and Kou’s own good, you know.
“It’s okay if you struggle, though. If you do, we’ll just be able to collect data on that, too.”

Saying things like that, the Doctor gave Sakura-chan and Kou a thorough examination. Perhaps thanks to Father staying by their side to calm them down, both Sakura-chan and Kou managed to hold their ground.
“Hmm, hmm. So this is the Filolial variant, then. I see.”
Saying that, the Doctor jotted down some notes.
“So, you mentioned you had business with me—what might that be?”
“Well, conducting health checks on Filolial in case of an emergency is a given, but there are various other matters as well.”
“So, Motoyasu-kun had business other than having Sakura-chan and the others examined?”
“Of course.”
You could even say that’s the main reason. After all, the Doctor is the best in that field.
“So, what do you want from Rat-san?”
“That would be Filo-tan, of course.”
“Huh…? Ah… I see. Sakura-chan and the others, please wait outside the room for a bit. Rasa-san and Werner, please.”
“Got it. You guys, let’s go.”
“What are you guys going to talk about?”
“Hmm?”
“Can’t Kou and the others listen in?”
“We’re going to be discussing something a bit complicated. It’ll be boring for you, so I’d like you to wait outside.”
I guess Father was being considerate—he shooed Sakura-chan and the others out. Then, with a slightly exasperated look on his face, he gestured with his hand for us to continue the conversation.
“So? What’s this all about, out of the blue?”
“It’s a long story, but it seems Motoyasu-kun has experienced the same period of time in this world over and over again—we call that a ‘loop.’ Actually, it seems he’s met Rat-san many times before.”
“That’s right.”

“It’s hard to believe at first, but I think I heard a little about it around the time of the Takt incident in Siltvelt—the one that started in Melromarc. The story about how the Spear Hero can foresee the future.”
“Yes, there were all sorts of complications with that matter…”
“What about that ‘Filotan’ you mentioned earlier?”
“Filotan is just Filotan, you know.”
“Motoyasu isn’t very good at explaining things, so please wait a moment.”
Father called me out on it. Well, it’s true that whenever I’ve interrupted him while he was talking, it’s almost never gone well. I guess I’ll just have to keep quiet, won’t I?
“So, here’s the thing. Motoyasu has a very important Filolial, and her name is Filo.”
“Hmm. How does that tie in?”

“It seems this girl named Filo is someone Sakura-chan might become in another loop. I think Motoyasu-kun came here to consult with Rat-san about how to turn Sakura-chan—who’s already grown up—into that girl named Filo.”
Wow, that’s Father for you. You’ve pretty much said everything I wanted to tell my Doctor.
“Exactly.”

“I wonder if I should be impressed by the Shield Hero’s insight—to figure that much out from such limited clues—or just be exasperated by the Spear Hero for suddenly throwing such a massive problem at me.”
“I’m sorry to spring this on you out of the blue…”
“It’s fine, though. After all, you’ve brought me a subject I’m somewhat interested in, and it looks like it could be an interesting case.”
Oh, it seems the Doctor is willing to go along with this.
“I’ve been feeling a bit stressed myself, so I need to blow off some steam with something interesting like this.”
“Did something happen?”
“Well, the Shield Hero and Spear Hero are indirectly involved, but I suppose you could call it the aftermath of the commotion surrounding the former Whip Hero.”
Takt, is it? Is that guy still causing trouble? I’m really getting sick of it.

“There was this guy from the Homunculus Research Institute—the one in the white lab coat who looked younger than his age—whom I considered a rival. As soon as he found out Takt had been killed, he abandoned his post and apparently took some equipment and ran off somewhere. And he’s still missing… or rather, is he on the run now?”
“The remnants of the Takt faction?”
“That’s right. Who knows where they fled to… Cleaning up their mess, handling requests for assistance from all sides—all sorts of things. For various reasons, Faubrey was in total chaos.”

I see… It really does hurt that we weren’t able to take down Takt properly. I suppose that just shows how large his faction is. The Doctor raises both hands in a visibly exasperated manner as she replies.

“Conferences and presentations will be postponed for a while. It’s been a nightmare. Well, I suppose it’s a relief that the commotion has calmed down somewhat, thanks to the Shield Hero and Spear Hero bringing an end to the war.”
“Really, they were treating the world as their personal fiefdom, weren’t they?”
“The quickest solution is to hunt them all down and kill them. That’s how it’s always been, and how it’ll always be.”
“Though advocating murder isn’t exactly a commendable thing to do…”
Father is such a kind man. Takt really ought to be grateful for this mercy, shouldn’t he? Well, knowing Takt, he’ll probably just trample all over it.
“So, going back to what we were talking about earlier—you mean you want to raise Filolial, who was born and raised here, all over again, right?”
“Yes. I think that’s the idea… Is there something you’d like to ask?”
Father asked, assuming something rather far-fetched.
“Hmm… Off the top of my head, I have one realistic idea. There’s also one that’s a bit of a pipe dream, but a hero might be able to pull it off.”
“Is there?”
“Though I can’t guarantee you’ll be satisfied with the result.”
“Please tell me anyway—I’d like to hear it as a reference, no matter what.”
“Alright, let’s start with the realistic one.”
Saying that, the Doctor crossed her arms again and replied.

“One option is to collect biological data from a girl named Sakura, create a homunculus or clone from it, and raise it. In short, it’s a method of creating a copy from scratch and turning her into a girl named Filo.”
“Ah… I see. I’m not exactly an expert on Ren, but I think I get the gist of it.”
“If you say it depends on how she’s raised and her environment, then as long as we can mimic those conditions, it should be possible to get pretty close, right?”
“This is starting to sound a bit insane, though…”
Father looks at me. So, we’re going to create a copy based on Sakura-chan and raise her to be Filo-tan? Hmm…
“So that means, if it goes well, we could create countless copies of Filo-chan, right?”
“In theory, yes. But… it’s going to be a pretty creepy sight. There are already so many Filolials as it is…”
“The catch is, the only way to verify if they’re genuine in terms of their souls is to have the Spear Hero observe them.”

Hearing the Doctor say that makes me wonder. Motoyasu, are you really satisfied with that? Would a Filo-tan created that way be the real thing? Is mass-producing fake Filo-tans what your idea of love is?
“That’s not it at all! Filo-tan is a one-of-a-kind being. She’s the only angel of love in this world.”
Even if there were countless Filo-tans, there’s only one real one. That’s my love.
“Well… that might actually be for the best. I wouldn’t want to see that either.”
“But then, that idea suddenly becomes completely unrealistic, doesn’t it?”
“What’s that idea?”
I’ll decide whether it’s realistic or not after I hear it. After all, having plenty of ideas isn’t a bad thing.
“Find or create one of those elixirs of youth you hear about in all kinds of stories, and have that girl take it until she turns into a baby bird.”
“Whoa… That does seem pretty unrealistic, doesn’t it? If you ask me, even being summoned to another world is on the same level as a work of fiction, so I can’t completely rule it out.”
“To a hero, this world itself is full of mysteries… That’s quite a difficult concept to grasp.”
“Motoyasu-kun, do you know anything about elixirs of youth?”
“An elixir of youth, you say?”

To be honest, I don’t know anything about such a potion either. Back when it was a game, it might have been a quest item or something, but I don’t remember the details that clearly. Ah, but I do remember something Father used to say.
“I don’t know if the one called the ‘elixir of immortality’ is true, but I do know of it.”
“He knew of an even more suspicious one. But it didn’t work out in the end, did it?”
“I see.”
“That said, I’m not giving up.”
“Not giving up is one of Motoyasu-kun’s strengths, but this particular situation…”

“Well, there’s one more option. It’s a pretty drastic method, but what if you made that girl Sakura lose her memory? We haven’t figured out exactly what criteria Filolial uses to determine their human forms, but if it’s based on her personality up until that point, it might work.”
“So you’re telling me to somehow make Sakura-chan lose her memory? That’s impossible.”
I can’t just go around needlessly injuring Filolial-sama. Even with Filo-tan, putting her to sleep on Father’s orders is about as far as I’ll go.
“Well, then, it’s out of the question. You’ll have to look elsewhere.”
